scenarios.prompt: White to move. Promote your pawn and keep the new piece: it must still be on the board after your opponent's reply. Every legal move is allowed; the computer plays the other side.
scenarios.explanation: The enemy king stands outside the pawn's square, so the pawn simply runs: push it every move and it promotes before the king can catch it. A pawn on its starting rank may move two squares at once.
hints: Count the moves: can the enemy king reach the promotion square before your pawn does?
Push the pawn at once. Every king move gives the defender a move to catch up.

scenarios.prompt: White to move. Promote your pawn and keep the new piece: it must still be on the board after your opponent's reply. Every legal move is allowed; the computer plays the other side.
scenarios.explanation: With your king in front of the pawn, the pawn promotes once your king reaches a key square two ranks ahead of it. Walk the king forward first, and push the pawn only when your king guards the square it moves to.
hints: Lead with your king: it clears the way and guards the squares in front of the pawn.
Push the pawn only when your king protects the square it moves to, or the enemy king can win it.

scenarios.prompt: White to move. Promote your pawn and keep the new piece: it must still be on the board after your opponent's reply. Every legal move is allowed; the computer plays the other side.
scenarios.explanation: When the kings face each other with one square between them, the side that does not have to move holds the opposition. Take it, with a king move or a spare pawn move, then step past the defending king to a key square in front of your pawn.
hints: Opposition: the kings on one file with one square between them, and your opponent to move.
A spare pawn move can give the move back to your opponent at the right moment.
